statement: Let $f(x) = x^2 - 6x + 5$. The graph of $y = g(x)$ is made by reflecting the graph of $y = f(x)$ across the $y$-axis and then shifting the result $3$ units to the right. What is the value of $g(1)$?

choices.misconception: I reflected across the $x$-axis instead of the $y$-axis, so I used $g(x) = -f(x - 3)$ and got $-f(-2) = -21$.
I shifted right $3$ to get $f(x - 3)$ but forgot the reflection, so I computed $f(-2) = 21$.
I reflected correctly to $f(-x)$ and then shifted right by writing $f(-x - 3)$, but replacing $x$ with $x - 3$ gives $f(-(x - 3)) = f(3 - x)$, not $f(-x - 3)$.

hints: Reflecting across the $y$-axis replaces $x$ with $-x$. Shifting right $3$ then replaces $x$ with $x - 3$ in the new formula.
After the reflection the function is $f(-x)$. Replacing $x$ with $x - 3$ gives $g(x) = f(-(x - 3)) = f(3 - x)$.

solutions.reliable: Reflecting $y = f(x)$ across the $y$-axis gives $y = f(-x)$. Shifting that graph $3$ units right replaces $x$ with $x - 3$: $g(x) = f(-(x - 3)) = f(3 - x)$. So $g(1) = f(2) = 2^2 - 6 \cdot 2 + 5 = -3$.
solutions.elegant: Follow the vertex. $f(x) = (x - 3)^2 - 4$ has vertex $(3, -4)$. Reflecting across the $y$-axis moves it to $(-3, -4)$, and shifting right $3$ moves it to $(0, -4)$. The parabola keeps its shape, so $g(x) = x^2 - 4$ and $g(1) = -3$.
